name: supply_chain_list_warehouse_restock_candidates
description:
List items that need restocking (a shipment in, or an assembly run) at the company's own NON-FBA fulfillment warehouses — 3PLs, own warehouses and locations that ship Shopify, wholesale, other-channel and FBM Amazon orders. Demand is total warehouse TURNOVER: invoice sales + outbound transfers (mostly FBA/AWD inbound shipments sent from the warehouse) + component consumption, so a warehouse that also forwards stock is replenished for both. One row per warehouse x top-level inventory item, ordered by priority (critical, high, normal, ok, no_demand) then ship_due_in_days ascending.

IMPORTANT — flat input: pass all parameters at top level. Required: company_id (integer).

SCOPE: only fulfillment warehouses — warehouses referenced by invoices (Invoice V1/V2 stock outflows) with sales in the last 90 days, excluding FBA/AWD/transit/Lost & Found. Use supply_chain_list_fulfillment_warehouses to discover warehouse_ids and their sales channels. FBA replenishment is covered by supply_chain_list_fba_replenishment_candidates; supplier PO timing by supply_chain_list_po_placement_candidates.

VELOCITY (sales_velocity, default 'current'):
  • 'current': realized invoice outflows at this warehouse, blended (w30*avg_30d + w7*avg_7d + w3*avg_3d) / (w30+w7+w3), default weights 0.5/0.3/0.2 (override with velocity_weighting). When the warehouse has no invoices for the item in the last 30 days but has some in 90 days (monthly or B2B invoicing), the 90-day average is used instead (velocity_basis = 'avg_90d'). ALWAYS tell the user which weights were used (meta.velocity_weighting_used).
  • 'planned': the channel sales forecast for the arrival month (today + lead time) x this warehouse's 90-day share of that channel's units (item-level share, else company-level), divided by the days in that month.
  • 'target': the item's daily_unit_sales_target.
Dependent (component) demand from assemblies built at the warehouse is always added: daily_sales_rate = mode rate + dependent_daily_units.

TRANSFERS (include_transfers, default true): stock shipped OUT of the warehouse to other warehouses (ledger App\\Models\\Shipment outflows at the origin; cancelled shipments never post). transfer_daily_rate = (transfer_units_30d/30 + transfer_units_90d/90) / 2 — independent of sales_velocity because transfers are large and infrequent. daily_turnover_rate = daily_sales_rate + transfer_daily_rate drives all outputs. transfer_rate_by_route shows the rate per destination warehouse; transfer_routes filters to items moving on any of the given routes (case-insensitive destination warehouse name, e.g. 'Amazon FBA US'). sales_channels and transfer_routes together keep items matching ANY of them.

DEMAND BREAKDOWN (include_demand_breakdown, default true): demand_breakdown lists the item's demand streams — sales channels (including channels that only have a planned share), transfer routes and component consumption — each with daily_rate, share, and its share of recommended_ship_qty / recommended_assembly_units. Stream rates follow the same sales_velocity and weights, so they sum to daily_turnover_rate and the allocated quantities sum to the recommendation. Use it to answer 'how much of this restock is for Shopify vs FBA'.
Sales channel per sale is inferred from the invoice's sales channel; velocity_by_channel shows 30-day units per channel and sales_channels filters rows to items sold through any of the given channels (case-insensitive).

PLANNING PARAMETERS:
  • lead_time_days: median replenishment lead time into the warehouse from shipment history (created/shipped -> arrived) and purchase orders (PO date -> received) over 365 days — item level when >= 3 events (source 'history_item'), else warehouse level ('history_warehouse'), else default 30 days ('default'). lead_time_days_override replaces it (source 'override').
  • safety_stock_days: default 10 days, flat in v1 (safety_stock_days_eff = safety_stock_days; ss_multiplier is returned for information only because the ABCD class is Amazon-revenue based). safety_stock_days_override replaces it (source 'override').
  • days_between_shipments: replenishment cadence, default 14.

MATH: available = on hand + in transit to the warehouse + open POs delivering to it; effective_available adds buildable units for assemblies built at the warehouse. rate = daily_turnover_rate. days_of_supply = effective_available / rate (99999 when rate <= 0). ship_due_in_days = floor(days_of_supply - safety_stock_days_eff - lead_time_days). need = max(0, rate x (lead_time + safety_stock_eff + cadence) - effective_available). recommended_ship_qty = need rounded up to box_quantity (0 for items assembled at the warehouse, which get recommended_assembly_units = ceil(need) instead). priority: no_demand if rate <= 0, critical if due <= 0, high if due <= stockout_threshold_days (default 7), normal if due <= cadence, else ok.

planning_base (default 'needs_replenishment'): 'needs_replenishment' = recommended_ship_qty > 0 or recommended_assembly_units > 0; 'actively_sold_only' = units sold at the warehouse in 30 days, component demand or outbound transfers; 'all' = every planned row. include_components=false drops rows whose planning_source is 'COMPONENT'. Each row includes the typical origin warehouse (most frequent shipment source) and its on-hand units to show where stock can come from.

warehouse_ids.description: Restrict to these fulfillment warehouse ids (from supply_chain_list_fulfillment_warehouses).

sales_channels.description: Keep items whose 30-day sales at the warehouse include any of these sales channel names (case-insensitive exact name match, e.g. 'Shopify').

transfer_routes.description: Keep items transferred on any of these routes in the last 90 days (destination warehouse name, case-insensitive, e.g. 'Amazon FBA US'). Combined with sales_channels as OR.

velocity_weighting.description: Blend weights for 'current' sales_velocity, normalized by their sum. Defaults 0.5/0.3/0.2 (30d/7d/3d). Pass {"weight_30d":1,"weight_7d":0,"weight_3d":0} for the plain 30-day average.

lead_time_days_override.description: Replace the history-based lead time for every row (lead_time_days_source becomes 'override').

days_between_shipments.description: Replenishment cadence in days added to the coverage target.

stockout_threshold_days.description: Rows with 0 < ship_due_in_days <= this value are priority 'high'.

include_components.description: When false, drop rows whose planning_source is 'COMPONENT' (items needed only as assembly components at the warehouse).

include_transfers.description: Add outbound transfers (stock this warehouse ships to other warehouses, mostly FBA) to the demand. false = sales and component demand only.

include_demand_breakdown.description: Return demand_breakdown per item (sales channels, transfer routes, component use with rate, share and allocated quantities).

daily_turnover_rate.description: Rate driving all outputs: daily_sales_rate + transfer_daily_rate.

daily_sales_rate.description: Sales rate for the selected sales_velocity plus component demand.
